messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired: PD-4321 — inference-queue depth high (us-west).
alert details: queue_depth=2,300 (5m avg) | enqueue_rate spike | autoscaler pending nodes > 10m | symptomatic 500s from router. See runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/inference-queue

pagerduty: PD-4321 acknowledged by alice (oncall)

alice (oncall): Ack, I'm on it. Looking at autoscaler logs now. First hypothesis: node provisioning is stuck at cloud quota/slow spot pool.

ben: I'm tailing the provisioner. Getting repeated errors: `QuotaExceeded: requested 8, available 0` when creating nodepool-usw2-hot. Also seeing `CreateNodeAPI 429` bursts.

carla: Can we temporarily divert traffic to dedicated-reserved-usw2? That pool has spare capacity. If we flip the gateway route we can shed new requests to dedicated and let the backlog drain.

alice (oncall): Good call. @carla can you prepare the route toggle? I'll coordinate with infra to manual-scale a small hotpool.

carla: Preparing gateway change. Command I plan to run:```
# flip primary inference route for non-enterprise
curl -X POST https://gateway.internal/route-toggle \ 
  -d '{"route":"inference","target":"dedicated-reserved-usw2","criteria":"priority!=enterprise"}'
```

dmitri: We should also throttle background batch jobs and low-priority customers to reduce enqueue_rate. I'll post a quick patch to the rate-limiter: `--max-concurrency 50` for batch-worker.

ben: Infra confirms cloud quota hit. I filed a quota increase request but approval ETA is 45m. Meanwhile manual spin-up of on-demand nodes is failing due to org-wide spot throttle. Trying a different instance family (g5->a10g) as fallback.

alice (oncall): Ok executing mitigations: 1) carla flip planned in 30s, 2) dmitri patching rate limits now, 3) ben attempting alt instance family. If gateway flip succeeds we'll monitor queue depth and tail latency.

carla: Route flip complete. Gateway returned 200. New traffic split: 60% to dedicated-reserved-usw2 for non-enterprise.

alice (oncall): Noted. Queue depth dropped from 2,300 -> 1,400 in 3m. Latency p95 for api-gen down from 1.8s -> 1.2s. Still seeing some 500s from the hotpath as in-flight KV caches are warming.

ben: Alt family spin-up succeeded for 4 nodes (a10g). They registered to cluster but kubelet reports slow kube-proxy sync; I triggered `kubectl rollout restart daemonset/kube-proxy` on the new nodes to finish join.

dmitri: Rate-limiter patch applied and rolled back partially for high-risk tenants only. Enqueue_rate dropped 40%. Good signal.

alice (oncall): Great. Handing off to ben for follow-up (node provisioning / quota ops). I'll stay tagged until queue < 200 and 500s resolved. If anything regresses escalate to @sre-lead.

ben: Will continue node health checks and liaise with cloud support on quota. I'll update this thread every 10m.

sre-lead: Thanks team. If quota approval stalls, prepare a plan B: 1) more aggressive traffic shedding for non-paid tiers, 2) temporary cached-response mode for embeddings where appropriate. Keep me in the loop.

alice (oncall): Customer impact summary (for postmortem): elevated tail latency for US-WEST customers, increased 5xx rate hitting < 1% of requests but concentrated on lower-priority tenants; no enterprise SLA breaches identified yet. Mitigations: gateway reroute, rate-limit patch, fallback node family. Root cause suspected: simultaneous spot pool reclamation + quota limit + autoscaler not failing open.

carla: Adding runbook note: update autoscaler to detect quota `429` and fallback faster to alternate families. Filed issue: https://redwood.internal/ops/issue/INFR-2199

alice (oncall): Closing active incident channel here. Will keep thread open for status updates. Last check queue_depth=180, p95=0.9s. Reopen if regresses. :white_check_mark:
